questions.question: Which relaunch flow do you want to live-test?

options.label: /relaunch a specific session
options.description: Pick a stopped/crashed cse_*, spawn a fresh bridge in its cwd seeded with its transcript brief. Original session not restored — new one starts from the brief as first turn.

options.label: Supervisor restart + fork
options.description: launchctl kickstart -k the supervisor; mm-* servers respawn from active-dirs.txt; then fork orphaned cse_ transcripts back in. Riskier — interrupts all live sessions on this host.

options.label: Both, in order
options.description: Restart supervisor first, then /relaunch one of the sessions that got killed, to verify the fork→relaunch path end-to-end.

transcript_tail.text: Are you able to relaunch and will the sessions be restored? I wanna do a live test now.

Quick check before I touch anything — "relaunch" is ambiguous here and the answer is different for each:

1. **`/relaunch <cse_id>`** — spawns a *fresh* bridge session seeded with a brief auto-derived from the prior session's transcript (cwd + branch + last N user turns). The original session is *not* resumed; you get a new `cse_*` with `vN` title bump and the prior context as its first user turn. Works for stopped/crashed/unresumable sessions.

2. **Restart the supervisor** (`launchctl kickstart -k …`) — SIGTERMs all `mm-*` servers, then they're respawned from `~/.ai-harness/active-dirs.txt`. Live `cse_*` sessions inside those servers are interrupted; orphaned transcripts on disk need to be forked back in *after* the new server is up (per memory).

Which one do you want to test?
